final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Metric-surface incident: GetAlerts shows LATENCY_DEGRADATION on the preserve-booking path only (ts-order-service p50 9.44ms->3881.58ms, ts-seat-service 17.65->3906.25ms, ts-security-service 39.11->3750.00ms, ts-travel-service p90 98.74->11000ms, ts-preserve-service p50 295.1->30000ms, ts-gateway-service p90 227.8->39000ms, ts-ui-dashboard p90 229.6->34500ms) plus a cluster-wide ~50-70% pps 'Network Drop' on every service. Object layer is excluded: all pods Running/READY 2/2, RESTARTS 0, nodes Ready with no taints/pressure, namespace events contain no mechanism Warnings (no FailedCreate/FailedMount/image-pull/scheduling failures), and no RESOURCE_SATURATION alerts exist (so not a resource fault). Call-graph arithmetic pins the fixed ~3.8s increment to ts-order-service: it is a leaf (no downstream calls, DB only), its own p50 jumps by exactly +3.87s, and its two direct callers ts-seat-service (+3.89s) and ts-security-service (+3.71s) inherit that same added delay, while deeper callers accumulate multiples (travel ~x3, preserve ~x8, gateway/ui ~x9-10). ts-order-other-service, called in parallel by the same callers (seat/security/preserve), shows NO latency degradation (only -37.8% pps), which excludes a delay on the callers' pods or on the worker-01 node network. Conclusion: a fixed network-path delay on the ts-order-service pod, with the front-end latency and global throughput collapse being downstream effects.

This wording lives on the metric surface — the alerts name the case, and the object layer is only the exclusion. Read the alerts first, and the case you land on decides:

1. **Alerts first.** `GetAlerts` tells you whose anomaly it is, which kind (latency / saturation / throughput / traffic), and at what scope. Unlike the reachability wordings, opening from the object layer here is not troubleshooting — the signal is in the metrics.
2. **Deal with the case you land on:**
   - **Saturation rows on one service** (`RESOURCE_SATURATION [cpu_cfs]` / `[cpu core]` / memory) → it's a resource fault on that service's pods: read its pods face (usage vs limits) to close.
   - **A constant delay riding on one service's own latency** — its p50/p90 jump by a fixed amount, its callers see the same added delay, its downstream server-side latencies stay clean, no saturation rows → `pod_network_delay`: the delay sits on that pod's network path. Don't reach for a code explanation — an artificial delay *in code* is a code-defect (a different wording, and it has to be shown from the code surface); under this wording a delay case is network-side.
   - **The same latency / packet anomaly across every pod on one node** (scope it with the pods listing's NODE column) → it's a node-scope network fault: read the node objects (conditions / node runtime services) to close.
3. **Close by excluding the object layer.** The pods / deployments / services / endpoints / nodes listings show everything else healthy — RESTARTS 0, AVAILABLE 1/1, endpoints bound, nodes Ready, no mechanism events. apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-service
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ts-order-service
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ts-order-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ts-order-service
        image: ghcr.io/sregym/ts-order-service:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        - name: SPRING_MAIN_ALLOW_CIRCULAR_REFERENCES
          value: 'true'
        - name: NODE_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: ts-order-mysql
        - configMapRef:
            name: nacos
        - configMapRef:
            name: rabbitmq
        ports:
        - containerPort: 12031
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 350Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        readinessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 12031
          initialDelaySeconds: 60
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-service
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 12031
  selector:
    app: ts-order-service
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-mysql
type: Opaque
stringData:
  ORDER_MYSQL_HOST: tsdb-mysql-leader
  ORDER_MYSQL_PORT: '3306'
  ORDER_MYSQL_DATABASE: ts
  ORDER_MYSQL_USER: ts
  ORDER_MYSQL_PASSWORD: Ts_123456
